note: Tester-facing captions for the web walkthrough, one entry per step in personas.json, in the same order. lead shows when the moment starts. outcome shows once the app has acted, or stayed quiet. title, where given, names the moment in the end-of-day summary when the step has no event of its own.

maya.lead: Maya's working on a cover letter for Bain. Her calendar says she has a coffee chat with a Bain alum in 15 minutes.
maya.outcome: Granola's open and ready before the chat starts.

maya.lead: Lunch is over and Maya has a group project meeting at 1.
maya.outcome: Nothing pops up. Maya has a notetaker now, so the coach stays out of the way. The menu bar shows what it noticed.

maya.lead: Maya's group presents at 4:30 and she's still on the slides.
maya.outcome: Slides are a real gap for Maya, but she already got a card today. This one waits in the menu bar so it doesn't interrupt her.

maya.lead: It's evening. Maya has an OCS mock interview tomorrow morning.
maya.outcome: Maya already has ChatGPT, so the coach wants to show her its voice mode for interview practice. She's still over today's limit, so this waits for tomorrow.

maya.lead: Next morning. The card that waited shows up at the first calm moment.
maya.outcome: ChatGPT opens in voice mode, ready for a practice run.
maya.title: OCS mock interview, the morning of

theo.lead: Theo keeps going back and forth between Claude and Figma.
theo.outcome: Now Theo can paste a frame link into Claude, using Figma's connector inside the app he already lives in.

theo.lead: Theo has seminar readings to get through before his 2 PM class.
theo.outcome: Theo already pays for Claude, so the coach shows him Projects, a part of it he hasn't used.

theo.lead: Studio review presentation at 5. Theo's in Keynote.
theo.outcome: Claude could have drafted the deck, but Theo would rather lay out his own boards. After Not for me, slide tools won't come up for him again.

theo.lead: Another presentation, this time practice for his final review.
theo.outcome: Nothing. Theo said slide tools aren't for him, and that sticks.

ines.lead: Ines has office hours with her professor at 11.
ines.outcome: Quiet. Ines turned off notetakers when she set the app up, and it respects that.

ines.lead: Seminar readings before her 1 PM class.
ines.outcome: Quiet again. She already uses Gemini Notebook for readings.

ines.lead: Her thesis chapter is due to her advisor at 5.
ines.outcome: Still quiet. She switched off writing help.
Apple's model reads this as a personal event, right on her Mac, so nothing happens.

ines.lead: Ines has a fellowship interview tomorrow afternoon.
ines.outcome: Big Interview opens. Yale's career office gives it to students for free. That was her only card all day.

dev.lead: Dev's Jane Street cover letter is due tonight.
dev.outcome: Dev installed Grammarly months ago and never opened it. The coach shows him how to use it here before suggesting anything new.

dev.lead: Dev keeps switching back to VS Code.
dev.outcome: Cursor's been sitting on his Mac unused. Another quick how-to, and nothing new to install.

dev.lead: Dev has a psych midterm tomorrow at 9.
dev.outcome: Gemini is the AI app Dev uses most, so the coach points him to Guided Learning inside it for studying.

grace.lead: Grace joins her study group on Zoom.
Still on the call. She has a coffee chat with an alum at 10:30.
grace.outcome: That's a real gap, since Grace has no notetaker. But she's on a call, so the card waits.

grace.lead: The call ends, and the card that waited shows up, ten minutes before the coffee chat.
grace.outcome: Granola's ready for the coffee chat.
grace.title: Coffee chat with Lisa, Class of '22, right after the call

grace.outcome: She has Granola now, so it stays quiet.
Study tools are a gap too, but she's had her one card today. This waits.
Another gap, another wait. Grace had several gaps today and saw one card.

rory.lead: Rory is writing a McKinsey cover letter and keeps pasting paragraphs back and forth between ChatGPT and Word.
rory.look: The coach takes a look at the letter, on the Mac. It keeps one line, "writing a cover letter for McKinsey in Word", and drops the picture.
rory.outcome: The coach has a tip, but it waits. Rory put off two cards while writing in Word last week, so it learned not to interrupt there.
rory.title: Pasting between ChatGPT and Word

rory.lead: Rory switches from Word to ChatGPT.
rory.outcome: Rory now has one prompt that gets feedback on the whole letter at once, in the app Rory already pays for. Nothing new to install.
rory.title: Leaving Word for ChatGPT

rory.lead: Rory is looking at an alum's profile. The calendar has a McKinsey coffee chat at noon.
rory.look: The coach takes a look at the page, on the Mac. It keeps that this is a profile and the role, and leaves out the person's name.
rory.outcome: Rory picked consulting as a career goal, so the prompt asks consulting questions, like how the alum got staffed on their first cases.
rory.title: Reading an alum's profile before a coffee chat

rory.lead: The coffee chat with the McKinsey alum is in 15 minutes.
rory.outcome: Nothing. Rory already uses Granola for notes, so there's no gap.
The coach didn't look. Passwords is on the never-read list, along with banking, messages, private browsing and password fields. Nothing pops up there either.
rory.title: Opening Passwords
rory.look: The coach checks its never-read list before it looks at anything.

rory.lead: Rory is reading the McKinsey job posting.
rory.look: The coach takes a look at the posting. It remembers the letter from this morning by its label only, not its text.
rory.outcome: Rory can now check the letter against the posting without letting ChatGPT rewrite it. That's three tips today and no new apps.
rory.title: Reading the McKinsey posting
